messages.author: f6d77eeabf5acd39
messages.subject: Specification of priors in blavaan
parts:
Hi all,


I have a question regarding the specification of priors in blavaan. I have a latent growth model, with an intercept and slope variable:


Model <- '

intercept =~ 1*x1+ 1*x2+ 1*x3

slope =~ 0*x1+ 1*x2+ 2*x3'


I would like to specify priors for the mean and variance of these two latent variables. To adapt the priors for the means, I understand that I have to change the alpha default prior, and for the variances I have to change the ipsi default prior.


Do I understand correctly that I can change the default prior for all parameters in alpha, but that I cannot specify a unique prior for the mean of the intercept, and a unique prior for the mean of the slope? If this is correct, do you know about another possibility to specify unique priors for the means of the intercept, and slope?


I hope someone can help me with this!


Sanne Smid

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Specification of priors in blavaan
parts:
Sanne,

You can change priors for individual parameters directly in the model syntax. See this page:

https://faculty.missouri.edu/~merklee/blavaan/prior.html

Ed

parts:
Hello blavaaners

I would like to specify priors for defined parameters (i.e. made with ":=" ). The page above didn't help and I could find out by myself.
Specifically, I want to set a prior to a difference in factor loadings and a difference in intercepts for different groups. I want to do this to find invariant reference indicators as suggested by Shi et al., 2017
This is a short version of how they do it in Mplus:

MODEL: %OVERALL% f BY x1-x9; [x1-x9]; x1-x9;

%c#1% f BY x1*(A1)
f@1; [f@0];

%c#2% f BY x1*(A2)
f*; [f*];

MODEL CONSTRAINT: new(Dif1-Dif18*0); Dif1=A1-A2;

MODEL PRIOR: DIFF(A1,A2)~N(0,0.01);

Their full Mplus code is in their appendix A( https://tandfonline.com/doi/suppl/10.1080/00273171.2017.1306432?scroll=top )

How can we mimic this in blavaan?

so far I've tried:
prior("dnorm(1,2)")*diff1 := A1 - A2

and also,

diff1 := A1 - A2
diff1~prior("dnorm(1,2)")*1

But blavaan couldn't read it.

Thanx in advance and congrats for the amazing package,
Victor

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Specification of priors in blavaan
parts:
Victor

This mplus code is for a multilevel SEM, blavaan is not able to do multilevel models yet.

You can do the approximate invariance between groups, the way to set the strong prior constraints is different but it achieve the same. The idea is that for group 2 you set mean of the prior at the estimate of the group 1, and set a small variance

for example, using JAGS in blavaan would look something like this

### configural invariance
mod1 <- '
Positive =~ PosAFF1 + PosAFF2 + PosAFF3
Agency =~ Agency1 + Agency2 + Agency3
            '

fit1 <-  bcfa(mod1, data=dat, std.lv=T, group="Gender",
            n.chains = 3, burnin=45000,
            sample=5000, target="jags", inits = "simple",
            bcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"))
summary(fit1, standardized=T,rsquare=T,postmedian=TRUE)
fitMeasures(fit1)   

with(parTable(fit1), cbind(lhs,op,rhs,pxnames)) ### find the JAGS names
### create variables L with the factor loadings for group1
factor_loadings_syntax <-"
L1 <- lambda[1,1,1]
L2 <- lambda[2,1,1]
L3 <- lambda[3,1,1]
L4 <- lambda[4,2,1]
L5 <- lambda[5,2,1]
L6 <- lambda[6,2,1]
"
## use the L variable as the mean for the priors for group 2
mod2_ap <- '
Positive =~ prior(c("dnorm(0,.01)","dnorm(L1,100)"))*PosAFF1 +
            prior(c("dnorm(0,.01)","dnorm(L2,100)"))*PosAFF2 +
            prior(c("dnorm(0,.01)","dnorm(L3,100)"))*PosAFF3
Agency =~ prior(c("dnorm(0,.01)","dnorm(L4,100)"))*Agency1 +
            prior(c("dnorm(0,.01)","dnorm(L5,100)"))*Agency2 +
            prior(c("dnorm(0,.01)","dnorm(L6,100)"))*Agency3

Positive ~~ c(1, NA)*Positive
Agency ~~ c(1, NA)*Agency
            '

fit2_ap <-  bcfa(mod2_ap, data=dat, std.lv=T,
              group="Gender",
              n.chains = 3, burnin=65000,
              sample=5000, target="jags",inits = "simple",
              bcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
              mcmcextra = list(syntax=factor_loadings_syntax) )
summary(fit2_ap, standardized=T,rsquare=T,postmedian=TRUE)
fitMeasures(fit2_ap)

Thank you Mauricio for this example of approximate MI in blavaan for multiple groups. Do you know if I can apply this approach to longitudinal approximate invariance as well? I've tried to specify a model similar to your example as a longitudinal model, but my estimates are way off/the model doesn't really seem to converge.

Here is part of my Rcode for a model with 3 time points (t1, t2, t3), and a scale of 5 items (x11, x12, x13, x14, x15 for t1). I am trying to estimate the first factor loading (By setting factor means to zero and variances to 1), but would be happy with a solution that fixes the first factor loading to 1 at this point.

factor_loading_syntax <- "

L1 <- lambda[1,1,1]
L2 <- lambda[2,1,1]
L3 <- lambda[3,1,1]

L4 <- lambda[4,1,1]
L5 <- lambda[5,1,1]"

intercept_syntax <- "
N1 <- nu[1,1,1]
N2 <- nu[2,1,1]
N3 <- nu[3,1,1]
N4 <- nu[4,1,1]
N5 <- nu[5,1,1]"

model2 <- "
t1 =~ NA*x11 + 
prior('dnorm(0, .01)')*x12 + 
prior('dnorm(0, .01)')*x13 + 
prior('dnorm(0, .01)')*x14 + 
prior('dnorm(0, .01)')*x15
t2 =~ prior('dnorm(L1, 100)')*x21 + 
prior('dnorm(L2, 100)')*x22 + 
prior('dnorm(L3, 100)')*x23 + 
prior('dnorm(L4, 100)')*x24 + 
prior('dnorm(L5, 100)')*x25
t3 =~ prior('dnorm(L1, 100)')*x31 + 
prior('dnorm(L2, 100)')*x32 + 
prior('dnorm(L3, 100)')*x33 + 
prior('dnorm(L4, 100)')*x34 + 
prior('dnorm(L5, 100)')*x35

t1~~1*t1
t2~~1*t2
t3~~1*t3

t1 ~ 0*1
t2 ~ 0*1
t3 ~ 0*1

x21 ~ prior('dnorm(N1, 100)')*1
x22 ~ prior('dnorm(N2, 100)')*1
x23 ~ prior('dnorm(N3, 100)')*1
x24 ~ prior('dnorm(N4, 100)')*1
x25 ~ prior('dnorm(N5, 100)')*1

x31 ~ prior('dnorm(N1, 100)')*1
x32 ~ prior('dnorm(N2, 100)')*1
x33 ~ prior('dnorm(N3, 100)')*1
x34 ~ prior('dnorm(N4, 100)')*1
x35 ~ prior('dnorm(N5, 100)')*1
"

Thank you for any guidance you may be able to provide!

Best,
Sonja

parts:
Sonja,

In principle, you should also be able to constrain the intercepts this
way. If the model runs but does not converge, you might try to set the
initial values by hand or use a higher precision on the "approximate"
parameters.

There is an example of setting initial values in Section 3.4 of the
blavaan paper:

https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v085i04

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Specification of priors in blavaan
parts:
Sonja

I have found the issue of convergence for approximate invariance with JAGS. I think this related to the Gibbs sampler behavior, makes it harder to converged on this type of models. With JAGS takes a long number of iterations t make it work. We recently worked an example on how to do this with Stan, in my experience the Stan sampler would deal better with these models here is a multiple group example, you can follow the same steps to translate it to longitudinal.

I teach a summer bayesian SEM course where I cover this type of issues and others, in case you interested https://www.statscamp.org/summer-camp/advanced-sem


library(blavaan)
library(rstan)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

### configural model
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school",
            target="stan", std.lv=T, mcmcfile = T)
summary(fit)

pt <- parTable(fit)

## figure out stan parameter names
with(pt, cbind(lhs, op, rhs, pxnames))

## or, if do.fit=TRUE above and you have the development version:
blavInspect(fit, 'stannames')

#### weak invariance. Using std.lv=T need to use lambdaUNC instead of lambda as the factor loading of the first group/time
hs2 <- '
visual  =~ prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[1,1,1],.1)"))*x1 +
prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[2,1,1],.1)"))*x2 +
prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[3,1,1],.1)"))*x3

textual =~ prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[4,2,1],.1)"))*x4 +
prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[5,2,1],.1)"))*x5 +
prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[6,2,1],.1)"))*x6

speed   =~ prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[7,3,1],.1)"))*x7 +
prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[8,3,1],.1)"))*x8 +
prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[9,3,1],.1)"))*x9

visual ~~ c(1,NA)*visual
textual ~~ c(1,NA)*textual
speed ~~ c(1,NA)*speed'

## test run
fit2 <- bcfa(hs2, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school",
             target="stan", std.lv=T)
summary(fit2)


blavCompare(fit, fit2)


## strong invariance
hs3 <- '
visual  =~ prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[1,1,1],.1)"))*x1 +
prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[2,1,1],.1)"))*x2 +
prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[3,1,1],.1)"))*x3

textual =~ prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[4,2,1],.1)"))*x4 +
prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[5,2,1],.1)"))*x5 +
prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[6,2,1],.1)"))*x6

speed   =~ prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[7,3,1],.1)"))*x7 +
prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[8,3,1],.1)"))*x8 +
prior(c("", "normal(lambdaUNC[9,3,1],.1)"))*x9

visual ~~ c(1,NA)*visual
textual ~~ c(1,NA)*textual
speed ~~ c(1,NA)*speed

visual ~c(0,NA)*1
textual ~c(0,NA)*1
speed ~c(0,NA)*1

x1 ~prior(c("", "normal(nu[1,1,1],.1)"))*1
x2 ~prior(c("", "normal(nu[2,1,1],.1)"))*1
x3 ~prior(c("", "normal(nu[3,1,1],.1)"))*1
x4 ~prior(c("", "normal(nu[4,1,1],.1)"))*1
x5 ~prior(c("", "normal(nu[5,1,1],.1)"))*1
x6 ~prior(c("", "normal(nu[6,1,1],.1)"))*1
x7 ~prior(c("", "normal(nu[7,1,1],.1)"))*1
x8 ~prior(c("", "normal(nu[8,1,1],.1)"))*1
x9 ~prior(c("", "normal(nu[9,1,1],.1)"))*1
'

## test run
fit3 <- bcfa(hs3, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school",
             target="stan", std.lv=T)
summary(fit3)


blavCompare(fit, fit2)
On Wednesday, May 15, 2019 at 10:28:59 PM UTC-5, Ed Merkle wrote:

Sonja,

In principle, you should also be able to constrain the intercepts this
way. If the model runs but does not converge, you might try to set the
initial values by hand or use a higher precision on the "approximate"
parameters.

There is an example of setting initial values in Section 3.4 of the
blavaan paper:

https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v085i04

Ed

>>
>> Victor
>>
>> This mplus code is for a multilevel SEM, blavaan is not able to do
>> multilevel models yet.
>>
>> You can do the approximate invariance between groups, the way to set the
>> strong prior constraints is different but it achieve the same. The idea is
>>
>> that for group 2 you set mean of the prior at the estimate of the group 1,
>>
>> and set a small variance
>>
>> for example, using JAGS in blavaan would look something like this
>>
>> ### configural invariance
>> mod1 <- '
>> Positive =~ PosAFF1 + PosAFF2 + PosAFF3
>> Agency =~ Agency1 + Agency2 + Agency3
>>             '
>>
>> fit1 <-  bcfa(mod1, data=dat, std.lv=T, group="Gender",
>>             n.chains = 3, burnin=45000,
>>             sample=5000, target="jags", inits = "simple",
>>             bcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"))
>> summary(fit1, standardized=T,rsquare=T,postmedian=TRUE)
>> fitMeasures(fit1)
>>
>> with(parTable(fit1), cbind(lhs,op,rhs,pxnames)) ### find the JAGS names
>> ### create variables L with the factor loadings for group1
>> factor_loadings_syntax <-"
>> L1 <- lambda[1,1,1]
>> L2 <- lambda[2,1,1]
>> L3 <- lambda[3,1,1]
>> L4 <- lambda[4,2,1]
>> L5 <- lambda[5,2,1]
>> L6 <- lambda[6,2,1]
>> "
>> ## use the L variable as the mean for the priors for group 2
>> mod2_ap <- '
>> Positive =~ prior(c("dnorm(0,.01)","dnorm(L1,100)"))*PosAFF1 +
>>             prior(c("dnorm(0,.01)","dnorm(L2,100)"))*PosAFF2 +
>>             prior(c("dnorm(0,.01)","dnorm(L3,100)"))*PosAFF3
>> Agency =~ prior(c("dnorm(0,.01)","dnorm(L4,100)"))*Agency1 +
>>             prior(c("dnorm(0,.01)","dnorm(L5,100)"))*Agency2 +
>>             prior(c("dnorm(0,.01)","dnorm(L6,100)"))*Agency3
>>
>> Positive ~~ c(1, NA)*Positive
>> Agency ~~ c(1, NA)*Agency
>>             '
>>
>> fit2_ap <-  bcfa(mod2_ap, data=dat, std.lv=T,
>>               group="Gender",
>>               n.chains = 3, burnin=65000,
>>               sample=5000, target="jags",inits = "simple",
>>               bcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
>>               mcmcextra = list(syntax=factor_loadings_syntax) )
>> summary(fit2_ap, standardized=T,rsquare=T,postmedian=TRUE)
>> fitMeasures(fit2_ap)
>>
